# Serenity

Hosted project memory for coding agents, with a free preview and a secondary open-source installation path. Hosted preview is for non-sensitive test memories while qualification continues. Paid subscriptions are not enabled.

- [Hosted plans](https://serenity.sire.run/pricing/): Free preview allowances and the planned Builder offer; not yet available for paid purchase.
- [Connect your agent](https://serenity.sire.run/docs/connections/): Client-specific token setup and explicit web-integration limitations.
- [Start free](https://serenity.sire.run/login): Email sign-in for a free hosted project memory.


- [Set up the brain. Work through your agent.](https://serenity.sire.run/get-started/): Install Serenity behind your agent or application. Start with a separate brain Git repository and a small set of sources.
- [Create your agent’s brain.](https://serenity.sire.run/docs/quickstart/): Create a separate brain repository, verify a small set of sources, then open your agent in that repository.
- [The brain behind your agent.](https://serenity.sire.run/product/): Serenity is a memory and context layer for agents and the systems you build. Your brain lives in a Git repository you own.
- [A clear path from install to useful.](https://serenity.sire.run/docs/): Set up a brain for Codex CLI, integrate Serenity into another system, and understand how context is stored and retrieved.
- [Bring your sources.](https://serenity.sire.run/docs/connectors/): Start narrow, verify what was imported, then expand your memory one source at a time.
- [Find the source. Then ask the question.](https://serenity.sire.run/docs/models/): Local search is useful on its own. Add model-assisted extraction and composition when you want cited answers.
- [Memory in your workflow.](https://serenity.sire.run/docs/workflows/): These commands are building blocks for your agent or integrating system. Run them directly when setting up or checking a brain.
- [Your memory. Your repository.](https://serenity.sire.run/docs/ownership/): Know what stays on disk, what can leave your machine, and what you need to back up.
- [Run behind your agent. Embed in your system.](https://serenity.sire.run/docs/agents/): Use Codex CLI in your brain repository, or connect your own system to Serenity’s memory and context interfaces.
- [Get back to the useful part.](https://serenity.sire.run/docs/troubleshooting/): Start with the smallest reproducible setup: one brain, one folder, and one known phrase.
- [Good questions. Plain answers.](https://serenity.sire.run/docs/faq/): The practical details before you add Serenity to your workflow.
- [Website and chat privacy.](https://serenity.sire.run/docs/privacy/): This public website helps you understand and install Serenity. It is separate from any personal brain you create.
- [Collected calm.](https://serenity.sire.run/brand/): A quiet identity for context that stays with its owner.
